standard_prerequisites.name: The class of the diagonal of a product as the intersection product of the pullbacks of the diagonals
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The identification of the diagonal of a product with the intersection product of the pulled back diagonals, together with the compatibility of the cycle class map with intersection products
standard_prerequisites.use: Expresses the class of the diagonal of the product through the classes of the diagonals of the factors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Definition of the degree map through pairing with the class of the diagonal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axiom (A6), defining the degree map as the pairing with the class of the diagonal
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the pairing of the lowest Kunneth component of the diagonal with the degree maps of the factors is one.

core_obligations: Reduce the multiplicative axiom (proof lines 4950-4954): the axiom concerning the behaviour under disjoint unions and the identity of the cohomology of the spectrum of the base is immediate from the identification of the cohomology of a product with the tensor product.

Compute the diagonal of a product (proof lines 4954-4983): the diagonal of the product of two schemes is the intersection product of the pullbacks of the diagonals of the factors along the projections, so compatibility of the cycle class map with intersection products expresses its class as the cup product of the pullbacks of the classes of the diagonals; decomposing these classes according to the Kunneth decomposition gives that the lowest component of the class of the diagonal of the product is the sum of the cup products of the pulled back components of the factors.

Conclude (proof lines 4983-4991): since the degree maps of the factors send the lowest components of the classes of their diagonals to one, the tensor product of the degree maps sends the lowest component of the class of the diagonal of the product to one, which is precisely the required multiplicative property.
proof_roadmap: Get the additive part of the axiom from the Kunneth identification.
Express the class of the diagonal of the product through those of the factors by compatibility with intersection products.
Pair with the degree maps to finish.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that axioms (A1) to (A7) imply axiom (B) on the behaviour of the theory under disjoint unions and products (statement lines 4946-4948). The proof (proof lines 4949-4991) derives the additive part from the Kunneth decomposition and verifies the multiplicative part by expressing the class of the diagonal of a product through the classes of the diagonals of the factors. H3: an explicit Kunneth computation, written out in full.
